description:
Companion connection to verify/part05-13-tickets, created from a two-reviewer critique of that manifest's first draft: part05-13-tickets' own RUNCOMBO only ever runs against CLEAN JUCHUD/JUCHUM data (its own expected/notes.md says '*PSSR は一度も発火しないはず'), so za0500-ticket3.rpg's actual *PSSR/QCMDEXC/CHGDTAARA code has never once executed in that connection - TXCHECK only proves the two objects exist/compile (its own header disclaims logic checking), and the OK/SHORT/NOTFOUND row check there only confirms ticket 1's fix. This connection instead DELIBERATELY corrupts a JUCHUD row (05-11's own C0511S technique, reused verbatim from verify/part05-mch1202-corrupt's own already-designed C0511RUN/C0511S/JUBADD staging steps - self-contained copies, per this repo's established per-manifest self-containment convention) and then calls the ticket-1-FIXED JU0900C (solutions/05-13/ju0900c-ticket1.clp) against the ticket-3 ZA0500 (solutions/05-13/za0500-ticket3.rpg, compiled AS ZA0500) - this is the first connection that gives za0500-ticket3.rpg's own *PSSR a real chance to fire from genuinely corrupted data, rather than from a hand-edited compile-time table the way ZA0510V forces its own (different) *PSSR in verify/part05-qcmdexc-runtime. Ticket 1 is fixed here (unlike part05-mch1202-corrupt, which deliberately keeps ticket 1 broken) so the MINQTY mismatch cannot fire first and mask the corrupted-JUSU error: za0500-ticket3.rpg's own C-specs run CHAIN -> Z-ADD AVAIL -> SUB JUSU AVAIL -> COMP MINQTY, all gated N90 in that order for one detail cycle (same static reading part05-mch1202-corrupt's own description already did), so with ticket 1 fixed, nothing in the C-specs competes to raise an exception before the corrupted JUSU's first use. Combined with C05119 sorting before every J-prefixed JUNO in JU0900C's own OPNQRYF KEYFLD((JUNO)(JULINE)) order (EBCDIC 'C' < 'J', same reasoning both sibling manifests already rely on), the corrupted row is expected to be the very FIRST row this connection's JU0900C/ZA0500 chain ever processes. UNVERIFIED, and deliberately left open rather than asserted (2026-09-27, advisor-flagged): exactly WHERE the corrupted JUSU first causes trouble is NOT settled by this static reading. verify/part05-qcmdexc-runtime's own actual hardware compile listing for this same source (ZA0500T3, work/verify/results/part05-qcmdexc-runtime-2026-09-26T23-43-17-905Z.json) shows JUSU cross-referenced as 'JUSU P(5,0)' - PACKED, not zoned - meaning RPG/400 converts JUCHUD's on-disk zoned field into an internal PACKED program variable during the INPUT phase (when the record is read), not lazily at first arithmetic use. If that input-phase conversion itself chokes on the corrupted bytes, the resulting exception could surface as early as the read/OPNQRYF-driven GET of the C05119 record - possibly as a query/file-class exception (a CPF50xx-shaped data-mapping error), not as a plain arithmetic decimal-data error at 'SUB JUSU AVAIL'. za0500-ticket3.rpg has no per-file INFSR on JUCHUD (only the program-wide *PSSR default-handler role, per its own header note), so if the failure IS a file-class exception rather than a calculation-time one, it is a genuinely open, unresolved question whether *PSSR's scope (explicitly framed around 'detail-calculation arithmetic (SUB/COMP/CHAIN with no 56-57 indicator)', per that file's own header) actually covers it - the header's own scope judgment explicitly excludes OPEN/CLOSE-time failures, but says nothing about a per-record read-time exception on an already-open file, which is a different case this session has not settled either way. This uncertainty is not a defect in this manifest's design - determining exactly which stage the error surfaces at, and whether *PSSR's scope covers it, IS itself the ticket-3 rubric's own '段階の特定'/'対象範囲の判断' items (docs/part05/05-13-checkpoint-tickets.md) - so expected/notes.md's reading guide treats BOTH outcomes (SUB-time decimal-data exception caught by *PSSR, or read-time file exception NOT caught by *PSSR) as legitimate, informative results, not as this connection having gone wrong. UNVERIFIED end to end: neither the C0511RUN->C0511S call nor this exact ticket1+ticket3 combination against corrupted data has ever run on real hardware before this manifest (part05-mch1202-corrupt, which shares the C0511S staging technique against the AS-SHIPPED, PSSR-less ZA0500, is itself still unrun as of this writing - connecting it FIRST would settle which message class the corrupted JUSU actually raises, more cheaply than this manifest alone can, since it has no *PSSR to potentially mask that message).

Judging success: the DEFINITIVE evidence is RUNVLDA3's own RTVDTAARA(*LDA (21 20)) readback (via the small compiled helper src/vlda3.clp, CALLed as the LAST step in this same wrapper job/call stack - *LDA is job-scoped, so a `collect` step running in a separate db2 connection after this job ends would only ever see blanks and prove nothing, the same reasoning verify/part05-qcmdexc-runtime's own VLDA already established). Expected value if za0500-ticket3.rpg's *PSSR fires and its own CHGDTAARA runs to completion: 'ZA0500 SHORT ERR' (16 characters) plus 4 trailing blanks, filling the declared 20-byte *LDA(21,20) range - see that file's own header note for the exact command text and byte math, and expected/notes.md in this directory for the full expected string. A SECONDARY, weaker corroborating signal (NOT the primary evidence, and explicitly an analogy from a different program, not a direct observation of za0500-ticket3.rpg itself): if the *PSSR fires and reaches its own ENDSR '*CANCL', RUNCOMBO3's own MONMSG around CALL PGM(&LIB/JU0900C) is expected to observe 'JU0900C: ZA0500 ended abnormally.' printed by JU0900C's OWN pre-existing MONMSG(CPF0000) around its CALL PGM(&LIB/ZA0500) - because verify/part05-qcmdexc-runtime's own actual (local, gitignored) hardware result already showed that the IDENTICAL ENDSR('*CANCL') mechanism za0500-ticket3.rpg reuses from za0510.rpg raises a genuine RPG-class escape ('Error RPG0000 caused program ZA0510V to stop.', vfylog) that a CALLer's MONMSG DOES catch - it does not let the program return to its caller unnoticed. That evidence is about ZA0510V, a different program exercising a different *PSSR trigger (a compile-time LOKUP miss, not corrupted runtime data) - it supports the GENERAL claim that ENDSR('*CANCL') raises a real escape, not the SPECIFIC claim that za0500-ticket3.rpg's own *PSSR will behave identically, so it is offered here only as corroboration, never as a substitute for the *LDA readback. Neither signal alone (nor together) distinguishes 'the *PSSR caught the error and ran CHGDTAARA' from 'something else entirely happened' as cleanly as reading *LDA back directly - which is exactly why this connection's design centers on RUNVLDA3, not on job-log message-hunting.

Steps, in the order this connection actually runs them (verify/lib/batch.mjs groups file/sh/cl/collect steps by TYPE regardless of JSON array position, so this ordering below is also the true execution order, not merely for readability): RUNTXRESET restores JUCHUD/JUCHUM/ZAIKOM to db/data/load_v1.sql's clean state FIRST (this connection cannot assume any prior connection to this shared dev-role &LIB left them clean, and the C05119-sorts-first reasoning above depends on no other stray JUNO value already sitting before it) - this deliberately undoes any corruption a PRIOR run of part05-mch1202-corrupt may have left behind in this same &LIB, which is fine (that sibling manifest's own description already documents leaving JUCHUD/JUCHUM corrupted on purpose and expects a future connection to TXRESET before assuming clean data - this is that future connection, for this &LIB's ticket-3 purposes, not a coordination promise). Then every object is (re)compiled fresh from its own source (DLTPGM-first, REPLACE(*YES), same self-containment/fail-visibly reasoning part05-13-tickets and part05-mch1202-corrupt both already use): C0511RUN, C0511S, JU0900C (ticket 1 fixed), ZA0500 (ticket 3's *PSSR, ticket 1's own ZA0500-side bug left as-is per that file's own header - irrelevant here since JU0900C now passes a correctly 5,0-typed MINQTY), VLDA3. The two collect steps (JUCHUD's own C05119 row incl. HEX(JUSU), and ZAIKOM's P00001 row) exist as a cheap secondary cross-check (was the row actually planted with the expected corrupted bytes; did RUNMODE='*TEST' really leave ZAIKOM untouched) - since collect steps run in a SEPARATE db2 connection after the whole CL wrapper job ends, they reflect the FINAL state after every cl step below has already run, not a 'before' snapshot. RUNC0511S plants the corrupted row (CALL PGM(&LIB/C0511RUN) PARM('&LIB'), the small LEN(200)-safe wrapper around C0511S - see that file's own header for why a bare CALL...PARM() literal would be unsafe here). RUNCOMBO3, the genuinely novel and riskiest step in this connection (this exact ticket1+ticket3-vs-corrupted-data combination has never run before), is placed LAST among the CALL steps that could plausibly still hang or misbehave, per README.md's hang-risk-last rule; CHGJOB INQMSGRPY(*DFT) at the top of every wrapper (verify/lib/clgen.mjs) auto-answers any inquiry message regardless, but this step stays last anyway as the documented precedent (part05-qcmdexc-runtime's RUNZA1V/RUNVLDA pair) already establishes. RUNVLDA3 - a trivial CALL to an already-reviewed-shape helper with no CALL of its own into any not-yet-run code - runs as the true LAST step, reading back the one piece of evidence this whole connection exists to observe. Prerequisite: TXSETUP has already built the sample DB in this library, same prerequisite as every other part05-* manifest; run from a branch where solutions/05-13/, src/qclsrc/c0511s.clp and this manifest all exist, not main.

2026-09-27 REVISION (real hardware, part05-mch1202-corrupt + advisor review): two findings from actually running part05-mch1202-corrupt against this same C0511S technique changed this manifest before its own first connection. (1) JUSU='ABCDE' (the value C0511S originally planted) turned out to be a VALID positive zoned-decimal encoding (EBCDIC A-E = X'C1'-X'C5', digit nibbles 1-5, sign nibble C) - it raised NO decimal-data error at all on real hardware (docs/probes.md), so this manifest's whole premise (a decimal-data error for *PSSR to catch) would not have held. FIXED: src/qclsrc/c0511s.clp now plants 5 blanks (X'40' per byte, an invalid sign nibble) instead - the classic real-world decimal-data-error trigger. (2) part05-mch1202-corrupt (which does NOT isolate JUCHUM) hit RPG1031 (JUCHUM match field out of sequence) before ever reaching SUB JUSU AVAIL, because JUCHUD is read in OPNQRYF-ascending order (C05119 first) while JUCHUM is read in arrival order (C05119 last) - the exact problem part05-mch1202-corrupt's own CLRJUCHUM step already isolates against. This manifest did not have a CLRJUCHUM step. FIXED: added CLRJUCHUM (RUNSQL DELETE FROM &LIB/JUCHUM, right after all compiles, before RUNC0511S) - same placement and reasoning as part05-mch1202-corrupt's own. Both fixes are unconfirmed on real hardware as of this revision; expected/notes.md updated to match.

steps.label: CPC0511RUN
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511RUN)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511RUN) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(C0511RUN) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPC0511S
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511S)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/C0511S) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(C0511S) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPJU0900C
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900C)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/JU0900C) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(JU0900C) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPZA0500
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTRPGPGM PGM(&LIB/ZA0500) SRCFILE(&LIB/QRPGSRC) SRCMBR(ZA0500) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.label: CPVLDA3
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB/VLDA3)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTCLPGM PGM(&LIB/VLDA3) SRCFILE(&LIB/QCLSRC) SRCMBR(VLDA3) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.sql: SELECT JUNO, JULINE, JUSHO, JUSU, HEX(JUSU) AS JUSU_HEX, JUTNK FROM &LIB/JUCHUD WHERE JUNO = 'C05119'
SELECT ZASHO, ZASU, ZAUPD FROM &LIB/ZAIKOM WHERE ZASHO = 'P00001'
